mainTopic: רבי יהודה and ברירה, why there is one stand on יום הכפורים, and the sprinklings in the היכל
overview: The amud opens by asking whether רבי יהודה accepts ברירה, the idea that a later choice can reveal what was true all along. A proof from the wine case is rejected, because there the worry may simply be that the jug could burst. A stronger proof comes from איו's ברייתא about a two-sided ערוב, and רבי יוחנן explains why the east-or-west case is not ברירה. With אין ברירה established, the גמרא asks why רבי יהודה does not allow two labeled stands on יום הכפורים, since he does trust writing. The answer is that the fasting כהן גדול is too weak to notice differences. He does not notice bowl size or blood color, so he would not notice a label either. רבא then corrects a חזן whose description of the עבודה mixed the views of the רבנן and רבי יהודה. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that the sprinklings in the היכל copy those inside the קודש הקדשים, and that the שכינה stays with ישראל even in their impurity. A צדוקי's challenge to that idea begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids drinking before separating, so he seems to reject retroactive clarification
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about wine bought from כותים ends with רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, and רבי שמעון forbidding the practice. The גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, and רבי שמעון forbid it. So it seems that there is no retroactive clarification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא and draws its point: since רבי יהודה forbids the practice, he must not accept ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wine case, a person wants to drink now and say that the portions he will separate later count as תרומה and מעשר right now. Relying on that requires ברירה: the later separation reveals which wine was תרומה all along. Since רבי יהודה forbids it, the גמרא infers that he rejects ברירה, which supports its explanation of why he worried about mixing up the coins.

keyTerms.meaning: They forbid
Apparently / this shows that
There is no retroactive clarification. A later choice cannot define what was true earlier.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the end of a ברייתא that the גמרא started quoting earlier, used here as a proof.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹסְרִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Shimon forbid it.
phrases.notes: They disagree with רבי מאיר, who permits it.

phrases.english: Apparently, there is no retroactive clarification.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is drawing this conclusion about what רבי יהודה holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא אֵין בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun earlier that רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about wine bought from כותים, where רבי יהודה forbids drinking before the separation

steps.title: The wine case may rest on a different reason: the jug might burst
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The rabbis there forbade the practice out of concern that the jug might split, not because they reject ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know that? Maybe that case is different, as the reason is taught there. They said to רבי מאיר: 'Don't you agree that the jug might split open, and he will turn out to have been drinking untithed wine all along?' He answered them: 'When it splits, we will deal with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It shows that the rabbis gave their own reason, a practical worry about the jug breaking, which has nothing to do with ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the jug bursts before he separates the portions, there will be nothing left to separate. It will then turn out that everything he drank was טבל. That is a practical risk, not a rule about ברירה. So רבי יהודה's ruling in that case tells us nothing about his view on ברירה. רבי מאיר answers that we do not worry about the jug breaking ahead of time.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?
Perhaps that case is different
Jug or skin container for wine
Produce that has not yet been tithed. It is forbidden to eat or drink.
Retroactively
When it splits (deal with it then)

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps it is different there,
as the reason is taught:
They said to Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה שֶׁמָּא יִבָּקַע הַנּוֹד
phrases.english: Do you not agree that the jug might split open
phrases.notes: Then the wine is lost before the separation happens.

phrases.english: and he will turn out to have been drinking untithed wine retroactively?
And he said to them: when it splits (we will worry then).
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר does not worry about the jug breaking in advance.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. It does not show that רבי יהודה accepts ברירה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling in the wine case rests on the practical worry that the jug might burst, not on a view about ברירה.

steps.title: A better proof: רבי יהודה forbids a two-sided condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings איו's ברייתא instead. רבי יהודה says a person may not make a condition about two things at once, which shows that he rejects ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from what איו taught. איו taught: רבי יהודה says, 'A person cannot make a condition about two things at once.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first proof failed, the גמרא brings a new and stronger source to show that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is an ערוב תחומין. A person wants to place an ערוב in two directions and decide on שבת which one counts, depending on which חכם he wants to hear. That needs ברירה: a later personal choice decides what was in effect from the start of שבת. רבי יהודה forbids this, and here there is no jug-type excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switching to a new proof)
איו, a חכם who taught ברייתות
Makes a condition
Two matters at once

phrases.english: Rather, the proof is from what Ayo taught.
As Ayo taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person cannot make a condition
about two matters at once.
phrases.notes: For example, an ערוב in two directions, where he chooses later which one counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִדְּתָנֵי אַיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 2 with a new one.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: איו's ברייתא about making conditions on an ערוב

steps.title: What is allowed and what is not in a conditional ערוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. He may make the ערוב depend on which direction the חכם comes from. He may not keep both directions open and choose himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if the Sage comes to the east, his ערוב is to the east. If to the west, his ערוב is to the west. But to here and to here (both, choosing as he likes), no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the line between an allowed condition and a forbidden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition that depends on an outside event is allowed, because only one חכם comes, from one direction. What is forbidden is a case where two חכמים come from two directions and he decides later which one to go to. There the result depends on his own later choice, which needs ברירה. That is why this case shows that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: His ערוב (the food placed to extend the שבת walking boundary)
East
West
To here and to here (both directions)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, רבי יהודה allows a condition that depends on outside events, but forbids one where his own later choice decides the outcome. That shows he rejects ברירה.
steps.confusionAlert: The east/west case is not ברירה being accepted. Only one חכם comes, so the outcome depends on an outside fact, not on his free choice.

phrases.english: Rather: if the Sage comes to the east —
his ערוב is to the east.
To the west — his ערוב is to the west.
But to here and to here — no.
phrases.notes: If Sages come from both directions, he may not choose later which one to go to.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִם בָּא חָכָם לַמִּזְרָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues Ayo's ברייתא and makes clear what kind of condition רבי יהודה forbids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition that depends on which direction a single חכם comes from is valid. A condition that leaves both directions open for his own later choice is not.

steps.title: Recalling why two open directions do not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion. A person cannot keep both directions open because רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: what is different about 'here and there,' where the ערוב does not work? It is because there is no ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes its own earlier discussion. That discussion explains the reason behind the ruling in step 4: a person cannot keep both directions open because רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving both options open would mean deciding later which ערוב was 'really' chosen from the start. That idea is called ברירה. Since רבי יהודה rejects it, the ערוב fails. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (the גמרא recalling an earlier discussion)
What is different? Why is this case treated differently?
To here and to there, meaning both options are left open
Clarifying afterward what was decided from the start

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
what is different about 'here and there' that it does not work?
Because there is no retroactive clarification.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא לְכָאן וּלְכָאן דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the ruling quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'here and there' ערוב fails because רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה.

steps.title: The east-or-west case should also fail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the case of one חכם who may come from the east or the west also looks like ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With east and west too, there should be no ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave. It asks why רבי יהודה allows the east-or-west ערוב, which also seems to depend on ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the east-or-west case, we only find out later which ערוב counts. That looks like the same kind of clarifying-after-the-fact. If רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, this case should fail too.

keyTerms.meaning: East and west
Also, too

phrases.english: To the east and the west
is there also no retroactive clarification?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב נָמֵי אֵין בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in step 5 by pointing to the case רבי יהודה permits.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that the east-or-west ערוב is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The east-or-west case also gets clarified later. If רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, it should be invalid too.

steps.title: The חכם had already arrived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the east-or-west case is one where the חכם had already arrived. The answer was already fixed and only unknown to the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: it is a case where the חכם had already come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. In the east-or-west case, the חכם had already arrived before שבת began. The person just did not know yet which side he came to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברירה means a choice that is truly still open and gets decided later. Here nothing was open, because the facts were already set and only the person's knowledge was missing. So רבי יהודה can permit this case and still reject ברירה in general.

keyTerms.meaning: When the חכם had already come

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'we did not know yet' is the same as ברירה. ברירה is about something not yet decided. Here it was already decided and simply unknown to the person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the conclusion safe that רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה. The next step builds on that conclusion.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is when the Sage had already come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּשֶׁכְּבָר בָּא חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the case is one where the facts were already fixed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The east-or-west ערוב depends on ברירה, just like 'here and there.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכם had already arrived, so it is not ברירה at all. רבי יהודה still holds אין ברירה.

steps.title: Then use two labeled stands on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: Even though רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה, he does rely on כְּתִיבה. So on יום הכפורים, why not set up two stands and label them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that we said רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה, he does accept writing! On יום הכפורים too, let us make two stands and write on them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the יום הכפורים case and asks a new question. If רבי יהודה relies on written labels, why not use two stands for the blood, each one labeled?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Confirming אין ברירה explained why רבי יהודה worries about mixing things up. But he trusts written labels, as we see from the labeled collection horns. Labels would solve the mix-up problem, so two labeled stands should be fine, yet he allows only one stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that we have said
Writing, meaning relying on written labels
He holds of it, he accepts it
Let us make two (stands)

phrases.english: And now that we have said
that according to Rabbi Yehuda there is no retroactive clarification,
he does accept writing!
On Yom Kippur as well,
let us make two and write on them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרִינַן לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֵין בְּרֵירָה, הָא כְּתִיבָה אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the confirmed אין ברירה and returns to רבי יהודה's ruling of a single stand on יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that there was only one stand for the blood on יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה trusts written labels. Labeling two stands would prevent mixing the blood of the bull and the goat, so a second stand should be allowed.

steps.title: The כהן גדול's weakness means he won't notice labels
steps.stepSummary: Labels would not help, because the כהן גדול is weak from fasting and will not pay attention to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the weakness of the כהן גדול, he will not pay attention to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8: why not set up two stands with labels? The answer is that the כהן גדול is too weak to notice the labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed writing would solve the mix-up problem. The answer says the problem is not a lack of information; it is the כהן גדול's tired, fasting state. A label only helps someone alert enough to read it.

keyTerms.meaning: Weakness (here, from fasting all day while doing the עבודה)
The High Priest
It is not on his mind; he won't pay attention to it

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי יהודה stopped relying on writing in general. Writing still works in other places. It just does not help here because of the כהן גדול's special condition on this day.

phrases.english: Because of the weakness of the High Priest,
it is not on his mind (he won't notice it).
phrases.notes: The writing on the stands would simply go unnoticed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם חוּלְשָׁא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל לָאו אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 (why not use two labeled stands).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical/situational limitation: the remedy works in theory but fails because of the person's condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Labels on two stands would prevent any mix-up, since רבי יהודה relies on writing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Labels are useless here because the weak, fasting כהן גדול will not pay attention to them.

steps.title: Proof: the bowls already differ in size
steps.stepSummary: If weakness were not the issue, there would be no mix-up even without labels, since one bowl is big and one is small.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, then even without writing there would be no mistake, since this bowl is large and this one is small.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its answer. If the כהן גדול were alert, he could already tell the bowls apart by size, so the worry about mixing them up only makes sense if he is too weak to notice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull has much more blood than the goat, so the bull's bowl is larger. Yet the משנה still worries about a mix-up. So something must stop him from noticing an obvious difference, and that is his weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (introduces a proof by showing the alternative doesn't work)
Large / more
Small / less

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then even without writing,
phrases.notes: There should be no confusion even with no labels.

phrases.english: this one is large and this one is small.
phrases.notes: The bull's bowl holds much more blood than the goat's.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 9 with a 'what if not' proof.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the כהן גדול's weakness keeps him from noticing differences.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The obvious size difference between the bull's and goat's bowls, which would prevent confusion if he were alert.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that he collects only part of the bull's blood
steps.stepSummary: One might say the bowls are equal because he collects only some of the bull's blood. But רב יהודה rules that all of it must be collected, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he does not collect all of it, didn't רב יהודה say: One who slaughters must collect all the blood of the bull, as it says, 'And all the blood of the bull he shall pour out at the base of the altar'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible escape from its proof. Someone could say the bowls are the same size, but רב יהודה shows that all of the bull's blood must be collected, so the bowl is bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 10 depends on the bull's bowl being bigger. A challenger could say only part of the blood is collected. רב יהודה's rule, learned from the word 'כׇּל' (all) in the פסוק, shuts that down.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
But didn't [he] say (introduces a source that refutes the suggestion)
Collects/receives (the blood in a bowl)
The base of the מזבח, where leftover blood is poured

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא לָא מְקַבֵּיל לֵיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: And if you say he does not collect all of it,
but didn't Rav Yehuda say:
One who slaughters must collect
all of the blood of the bull,
as it is said: "And all the blood of the bull
he shall pour out at the base of the altar."
phrases.notes: This is ויקרא 4:7. Since it says 'all' the blood, all of it must be collected.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא לָא מְקַבֵּיל לֵיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the proof of step 10 against a possible counter-argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that the bowls could be equal because only part of the bull's blood is collected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against רב יהודה's rule, based on a פסוק, that all of the bull's blood must be collected.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that spilled blood makes them equal
steps.stepSummary: Even if some bull blood spilled and the amounts became equal, the colors still differ: one is pale, the other red.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say perhaps some of it spilled out, still this one is pale and this one is red.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a second escape. Even if spilling made the amounts equal, he could still tell them apart by color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Size is not the only visible difference. The goat's blood is lighter and the bull's blood is darker. So an alert person would still never confuse them, which again means the real problem is his weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
Spills out
Pale/whitish (the goat's blood)
Red (the bull's blood)

phrases.english: And if you say: perhaps some of it spills out,
phrases.notes: So the two amounts might end up equal.

phrases.english: still, this one is pale and this one is red.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: דִּילְמָא מִשְׁתְּפִיךְ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second defense of the proof, after step 11 handled the first counter-argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that spilling makes the bloods impossible to tell apart.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two bloods still look different in color, so an alert person could not confuse them.

steps.title: Conclusion: weakness explains it, and labels won't help either
steps.stepSummary: The only explanation is the כהן גדול's weakness, and the same reason shows why labeled stands would not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because of the weakness of the כהן גדול, he does not pay attention. Here too, because of his weakness, he will not pay attention to the writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up. Since size and color are not enough to prevent a mix-up, it must be his weakness, and that same weakness makes labels useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof showed that obvious visual differences do not help him. So a written label, which is less obvious than size or color, certainly will not help. This fully answers the question from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the only remaining explanation)
Here too (applies the same reasoning to the current case)

steps.whatToRemember: There is one stand, not two labeled ones, because the fasting כהן גדול is too weak to notice differences. He does not notice bowl size or blood color, so he would not notice a written label either.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יהודה's acceptance of writing as a solution has a practical limit. Writing only helps when the person is in a state to pay attention.

phrases.english: Rather, because of the weakness of the High Priest,
it (size and color) is not on his mind.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, מִשּׁוּם חוּלְשָׁא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: Here too, because of the weakness of the High Priest,
it (the writing) is not on his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִשּׁוּם חוּלְשָׁא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל לָאו אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof from steps 10–12 and applies it back to the question of step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two labeled stands would not prevent a mix-up, because the כהן גדול's weakness keeps him from noticing any distinguishing sign, whether size, color, or writing.

steps.title: A prayer leader before רבא recites the order of the service
steps.stepSummary: A חזן leading the prayers before רבא described the כהן גדול placing the bowl on the second stand, taking the bull's blood, and putting down the goat's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain person went down to lead the prayers before רבא and said: He went out and put it on the second stand in the היכל, took the bull's blood, and put down the goat's blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. It is setting up a case so that רבא can react to how the חזן described the order of the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזן's wording speaks of a 'second stand' (two stands) and describes taking up the bull's blood while setting down the goat's blood. This order of actions will be examined in the next step, which is where רבא responds.

keyTerms.meaning: Who went down before him (to lead the prayers as חזן)
A stand/pedestal for the bowl of blood
The Sanctuary, the room outside the קודש הקדשים
The goat (offered on יום הכפורים)

phrases.english: A certain person who went down (to lead prayers) before Rava
phrases.notes: The חזן stood in a lower spot in front of the ark.

phrases.english: said: He went out and placed it
on the second stand in the Sanctuary,
took the blood of the bull,
and put down the blood of the goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the conclusion in step 13; the story continues next with רבא's response.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A recited version of the עבודה describing two stands and the order of picking up the bull's blood and putting down the goat's blood, set up for רבא's reaction.

steps.title: רבא points out a mixed-up description
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the חזן's description mixes two opinions: part follows the רבנן and part follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You said one thing like the רבנן and one thing like רבי יהודה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the חזן's wording. Half of it follows the רבנן and half follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזן said the bowl was put on a 'second stand.' That only fits the רבנן, who say there were two stands. Then he said 'took the bull's blood, then put down the goat's blood.' That order fits רבי יהודה, who says there was only one stand, so the כהן גדול had to pick up one bowl before he could put down the other. One description cannot follow both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: One (here: one part of the statement)
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the act itself. The problem is the ORDER of the words. 'Take, then put down' is only needed if there is one stand. With two stands, he can put one bowl down first.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: one is like the Rabbis
phrases.notes: The part about the 'second stand' follows the רבנן, who hold there were two stands.

phrases.english: and one is like Rabbi Yehuda?!
phrases.notes: Taking first and then putting down follows רבי יהודה, who holds there was one stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדָא כְּרַבָּנַן וַחֲדָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording the חזן used in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חזן's description of the order of placing and taking the bowls.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The description is inconsistent. 'Second stand' assumes the רבנן's two stands, but 'took, then placed' assumes רבי יהודה's single stand.

steps.title: רבא's corrected wording
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells the חזן to say: 'he placed the goat's blood, and took the bull's blood,' which fits the רבנן all the way through.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: He placed down the goat's blood, and then took the bull's blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא fixes the wording so the whole description follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two stands there is room to put the goat's blood down first and only then pick up the bull's blood. Switching the order removes the part that came from רבי יהודה. Now the whole description is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (instead); a fix to the wording
He placed down
He took

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן there are two stands. So the כהן גדול puts down the goat's blood first and then picks up the bull's blood.

phrases.english: Say: he placed the blood of the goat,
phrases.notes: First he puts the goat's blood on its own stand.

phrases.english: and took the blood of the bull.
phrases.notes: Then he lifts the bull's blood from the other stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: הִנִּיחַ דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר, וְנָטַל דַּם הַפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the problem raised in Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חזן's order (take, then place) could stand as said.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order must be place, then take, so it follows the רבנן consistently.

steps.title: The משנה: sprinkling toward the curtain from outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the כהן גדול sprinkled the bull's blood on the פרוכת, facing the ארון, from outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he sprinkled from it on the curtain, opposite the Ark, from outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the sprinklings were inside the קודש הקדשים. Now the כהן גדול stands in the היכל and sprinkles toward the פרוכת, lined up with where the ארון is behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he sprinkled
The curtain between the היכל and the קודש הקדשים
The Ark
From outside (in the היכל)

phrases.english: And he sprinkled from it on the curtain
phrases.notes: 'From it' means from the bull's blood.

phrases.english: opposite the Ark, from outside.
phrases.notes: He stands in the היכל, outside the קודש הקדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ עַל הַפָּרוֹכֶת כְּנֶגֶד אָרוֹן מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bull's blood is sprinkled toward the פרוכת, facing the ארון, from the היכל side.

steps.title: What does 'so shall he do for the אהל מועד' teach?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what we learn from the words 'and so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting.' What does this verse come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא asks what these words of the פסוק add. This sets up its answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'so' (וְכֵן) tells us the היכל service copies something. The question is what exactly it copies. The answer will be the source for the sprinklings in the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: Tent of Meeting; here, the היכל
What does the verse come to teach?

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:טז

phrases.english: what does the verse come to teach?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the פסוק that is the source of the משנה's sprinkling in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'so' (וְכֵן) teaches about the service in the היכל.

steps.title: The היכל sprinklings copy the inner ones
steps.stepSummary: Just as he sprinkles inside the קודש הקדשים (one up, seven down), he sprinkles the same way in the היכל. This applies to both the bull's blood and the goat's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as he sprinkles in the innermost place, so he sprinkles in the היכל. Just as inside it is one upward and seven downward from the bull's blood, so he sprinkles in the היכל. And just as inside it is one upward and seven downward from the goat's blood, so he sprinkles in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: 'so' means the היכל sprinklings follow the same pattern as the ones in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It teaches two things. First, there is sprinkling in the היכל at all. Second, it has the same count and style: one upward and seven downward, done separately for the bull and for the goat.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost place; the קודש הקדשים
The Sanctuary, outside the פרוכת
One sprinkling upward and seven downward

steps.whatToRemember: In the היכל the כהן גדול does exactly what he did inside: 1 up + 7 down from the bull, then 1 up + 7 down from the goat, all toward the פרוכת.

phrases.english: Just as he sprinkles in the innermost place —
so he sprinkles in the Sanctuary.
Just as in the innermost place,
once upward and seven downward
from the blood of the bull —
so he sprinkles in the Sanctuary.
And just as in the innermost place,
once upward and seven downward
from the blood of the goat —
so he sprinkles in the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּזֶּה לִפְנַי לְפָנִים כָּךְ מַזֶּה בַּהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'So' teaches that the sprinklings in the היכל match the inner ones: one up and seven down, for the bull and for the goat.

steps.title: The שכינה stays even in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The end of the פסוק, 'that dwells with them in the midst of their impurity,' teaches that the שכינה is with ישראל even when they are טמאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That dwells with them in the midst of their impurity': even at a time when they are impure, the שכינה is with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the last words of the same פסוק. They teach that the שכינה does not leave ישראל when they become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new lesson, not about the order of sprinklings. The פסוק says ה׳ dwells 'in the midst of their impurity.' The ברייתא reads this to mean that the שכינה stays even while ישראל are טמאים.

keyTerms.meaning: That dwells
Their impurity
The Divine Presence

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea is what the צדוקי will challenge in the next step, so it sets up the coming story.

phrases.english: 'That dwells with them in the midst of their impurity,'
even at a time when they are impure —
the Divine Presence is with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טוּמְאֹתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains another part of the same פסוק used in Steps 18-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה remains with ישראל even when they are impure.

steps.title: A צדוקי speaks to רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: a certain צדוקי said something to רבי חנינא about this idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain צדוקי said to רבי חנינא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a story whose content comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקי is about to challenge the idea that the שכינה stays with ישראל in their impurity. The actual challenge and רבי חנינא's answer come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sadducee; one who rejects the Oral Torah

phrases.english: A certain Sadducee said
to Rabbi Ḥanina:
phrases.notes: The words of the challenge continue on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא צַדּוּקִי לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a story about the lesson taught in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a story; the content follows on the next amud.
